title: Bulk electronic heat–charge decoupling sufficient for engine-class solid-state conversion

concept.text: The proposed innovation is a bulk, manufacturable thermoelectric material system that carries electrical current well while allowing unusually little heat to travel with its charge carriers. Thermoelectric generators convert a temperature difference into electricity without moving parts. Their charge carriers also conduct heat, which can drain the temperature difference needed for conversion. The target is to weaken this electronic heat leakage substantially while retaining a high electrical power factor, S²σ, where S is the Seebeck coefficient and σ is electrical conductivity.

As a proposed capability, this extends from transport physics to a complete generator: compatible positive-type and negative-type thermoelectric legs, fabricated as stable bulk solids and assembled into a module that delivers high efficiency at useful electrical power density. An isolated low Lorenz number, an exceptional single leg, or a material-level improvement would establish only part of the concept. The supplied evidence does not establish that the complete capability has been achieved.

significance.text: The transport constraint can be stated precisely. Electronic thermal conductivity is written κe = LσT, with L the electronic Lorenz number and T absolute temperature. Thermoelectric performance is characterized by ZT = S²σT/(κe + κl), where κl is lattice thermal conductivity. If lattice heat conduction vanishes, this becomes ZT = S²/L. When L remains near the Sommerfeld reference value, suppressing lattice conduction alone therefore leaves a limit that depends on the Seebeck coefficient. It is not a universally modest ceiling: its magnitude depends on S. Strongly reducing L while retaining S and σ could relax this electronic constraint.

Conditional significance: if this transport improvement survived bulk fabrication and enabled complete modules to convert heat at a large fraction of Carnot efficiency while delivering useful power, it would create a consequential solid-state option for industrial heat conversion and waste-heat recovery. The direct advance would be less electronic heat leakage for a given useful electrical response. Broader competition with mechanical heat engines would additionally depend on fabrication cost, heat exchangers, material availability, operating conditions and system durability.

Lower Lorenz number alone would not guarantee that outcome. Lattice heat flow can remain substantial; changes that suppress electronic heat conduction can also damage electrical conductivity or the Seebeck coefficient. Both thermoelectric legs must perform across the temperature span, and interfaces and connections introduce losses. The supplied module analysis supports evaluating the assembled device rather than treating one material's peak ZT as its generator's performance.

Scope limitation: this concept concerns thermoelectric transport and does not establish a ranking against thermophotovoltaic conversion. The supplied evidence does not substantiate either the earlier claim that thermophotovoltaic cells had exceeded 40 percent efficiency or the judgment that their remaining system-engineering challenge is weaker. Such a comparison would require separate evidence and matched operating and measurement boundaries.

missing_breakthrough.text: The target breakthrough is strong, reproducible suppression of electronic thermal conductivity relative to the Sommerfeld Wiedemann–Franz reference in a bulk conductor, while preserving a high power factor at generator operating temperatures. It must persist through fabrication and sustained operation. The supplied evidence motivates this target but does not establish the prevalence, magnitude or operating regimes of known Lorenz-number violations, nor whether the complete target remains unmet as of November 1, 2026.

A central measurement barrier is identifying electronic heat conduction independently of lattice heat flow and other contributions. Because L is inferred from κe/(σT), uncertainty in separating κe from total thermal conductivity can create an apparent suppression. A convincing result must explain that separation, quantify uncertainty and check for measurement artifacts. The research describes a relevant Lorenz-number study, but its source text was not retained in the supplied record, so that study's particular mechanism and artifact analysis cannot be treated as verified here.

The device barrier is obtaining compatible P- and N-type legs with favorable temperature-dependent properties, then preserving their advantage through contacts, interconnects and thermal insulation. Ryu and colleagues' analysis emphasizes simultaneous development of both legs and the effects of parasitic electrical and thermal resistance. Translating the concept into a practical generator also requires stable bulk processing and repeatable fabrication, rather than favorable transport in a specially prepared specimen alone.

current_state.text: The supplied review verifies an arXiv record identifying Byungki Ryu and eight coauthors and linking their work to Journal of Applied Physics 137, 115001 (2025), DOI 10.1063/5.0247466. The technical text reviewed was the retained November 2024 preprint, not an independently inspected full journal version. Its 24-page text, including supporting material, was available to the reviewer; figure images were not inspected. The landing page supplied bibliographic and abstract information.

Within the Constant Seebeck-coefficient Approximation, that preprint derives that an optimized P-N module's effective ZT lies between the values of its constituent legs. This does not mean that module effective ZT is necessarily below both legs' values. It separately identifies substantial additional electrical and thermal losses in a single-leg device through its hot-side connecting wire. These are analytical constraints on interpreting material and device performance, rather than a demonstration of the proposed heat–charge decoupling capability.

The reconciled research attributes a result to Gao and colleagues in Science 390, 1266–1271, dated December 18, 2025, DOI 10.1126/science.adt0831. It reports that the editor's summary and abstract described n-type SnSe with average ZT of about 3.0 from 673 to 923 K and conversion efficiency of about 19.1 percent at a temperature difference of about 572 K. These figures and bibliographic details are preserved as reports from the earlier research: no Science page text or article artifact was supplied for the validated review, so they could not be checked there. The full byline and the efficiency experiment's device configuration, measurement boundary and absolute terminal temperatures remain unverified in this record.

The reported 572 K temperature difference alone cannot establish how 19.1 percent compares with half of Carnot efficiency. Carnot efficiency is 1 − Tc/Th and requires absolute hot- and cold-side temperatures. The reported 673–923 K interval for average material ZT should not be assumed to supply the terminals of the efficiency experiment. Even if the reported performance is confirmed, those figures alone would not establish independently measured electronic Lorenz suppression or the complete module capability defined here.

The earlier research also describes a November 2025 Nature Communications article titled “Hidden in plain heat: anomalous Lorenz number in the thermoelectric alloy Bi0.4Sb1.6Te3.” It attributes anomalously low Lorenz number to inelastic scattering and describes a warning about artifacts in some very-low-Lorenz-number claims. The earlier pass reportedly read a DOAJ abstract index, but neither that index text nor the underlying article was retained for the validated review. Its publication details, mechanism and measurement interpretation therefore remain unverified here. The earlier attribution to Garmroudi and coauthors was withdrawn, and no replacement author attribution is established.

The supplied evidence establishes relevant transport reasoning and module constraints, but does not settle the field's latest experimental position. The freshness record contains no search entries, and the two reported 2025 experimental sources lack retained text. Consequently, this record cannot establish whether a bulk module already combines large, confirmed electronic Lorenz suppression with engine-class efficiency as of November 1, 2026. Those evidence gaps neither demonstrate achievement nor show that the reported results are false.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed demonstration: fabricate a polycrystalline P-N module whose two legs each have an independently measured electronic Lorenz number below one-third of the Sommerfeld value at the hot-side operating temperature, and demonstrate module efficiency above half of Carnot between measured absolute terminal temperatures. These numerical thresholds are proposed milestones for this concept, not established scientific or engineering standards.
completion_criteria.label: Proposed demonstration

completion_criteria.text: Measure and report transport properties across the full operating temperature span, including Seebeck coefficient, electrical conductivity, total thermal conductivity and the method used to separate electronic heat flow. A hot-side Lorenz measurement alone cannot establish suppression throughout the module. Report uncertainty and independent checks sufficient to distinguish electronic suppression from an erroneous allocation of heat conduction.
completion_criteria.label: Measure and report transport properties across the full

completion_criteria.text: Use a declared module measurement boundary that includes contact and insulation losses, with explicit accounting for interconnects and other relevant parasitic heat and electrical paths. Measure electrical output power and heat input under the same operating conditions. The need to distinguish complete-module performance from constituent-leg performance is grounded in Ryu and colleagues' analysis; this measurement protocol is a proposal for demonstrating the present concept.
completion_criteria.label: Use a declared module measurement boundary that includes

completion_criteria.text: Proposed durability and reproducibility test: sustain operation for 1,000 hours at the declared temperatures with no efficiency degradation exceeding a stated measurement uncertainty. Repeat the transport and module results across independently fabricated batches and seek independent laboratory replication. Report fabrication method, yield, module dimensions, power density and material requirements so that manufacturability and practical output can be assessed. The present proposal specifies no numerical minimum for power density, fabrication yield or cost; those boundaries remain to be defined for a chosen application.
completion_criteria.label: Proposed durability and reproducibility test

completion_criteria.text: A successful test would establish performance over the tested temperatures, loads, fabrication batches and duration. It would not demonstrate universal heat–charge decoupling, indefinite lifetime or competitiveness across all heat-engine applications. Those broader claims would require additional operating envelopes and system-level comparisons.

related_concepts.text: Roster-based synthesis: THR-02, “Useful heat engines that are simultaneously efficient, powerful, and steady,” is the closest performance-level neighbor. THR-04 proposes a particular solid-state transport route toward that broader combination. High thermoelectric efficiency alone would not establish THR-02's full conjunction unless useful power and steady operation were also demonstrated.

Roster-based synthesis: THR-01, “A computable thermodynamic potential for far-from-equilibrium continuum transport,” and THR-11, “Operational temperature and entropy for far-from-equilibrium matter,” concern broader theoretical descriptions. They could inform transport modeling or interpretation, but THR-04 specifically requires a material and module capability; it does not require either general theoretical program to be completed.

Roster-based synthesis: THR-05, “A size-extensive quantum advantage in thermodynamic performance,” could overlap if a quantum mechanism produced scalable transport benefits. THR-04 does not require a demonstrated quantum advantage. THR-06, “A single-absorber solar converter that uses non-thermal carriers to pass the detailed-balance limit,” also concerns energy conversion through carrier physics, but its solar absorption and non-thermal-carrier target differs from suppressing electronic heat leakage in a thermoelectric generator.

Roster-based synthesis: THR-03, “General-purpose digital computation near the Landauer scale,” and THR-08, “Equilibrium sampling computers operating near thermal energy per sample,” concern the thermodynamic cost of computation. Their shared interest in heat and energy efficiency does not make them thermoelectric conversion concepts. THR-04 targets electrical generation from a temperature difference.

Roster-based synthesis: THR-07, “Synthetic chemomechanical engines whose efficiency approaches biological molecular motors,” targets chemical-to-mechanical conversion. THR-09, “A thermodynamic design theory of self-replicators, confirmed by a predicted non-biological replicator,” and THR-12, “Predictive thermodynamic design of far-from-equilibrium chemical reaction networks,” target chemical organization and predictive design. They share thermodynamic performance questions with THR-04 while retaining distinct mechanisms and demonstrations.

Roster-based synthesis: THR-10, “A laboratory measurement of the Unruh temperature,” concerns a fundamental temperature measurement rather than bulk transport engineering. Its connection to THR-04 is thematic, through thermodynamics, and it supplies no completion criterion for this innovation.

change_log.change: Preserved THR-04's identity and expanded its definition from material transport to a complete bulk P-N generator.
change_log.reason: The research supplies the intended breakthrough, while the review explains why both legs and module losses are essential to demonstrating it.

change_log.change: Replaced the universal-sounding modest ZT ceiling with the conditional relation ZT = S²/L when lattice conduction vanishes.
change_log.reason: The ceiling depends on the Seebeck coefficient and the stated transport assumptions.

change_log.change: Removed categorical claims about the prevalence of known Lorenz violations and the present absence of a qualifying module.
change_log.reason: The supplied evidence does not survey those violations or establish field-wide absence, and the freshness record is empty.

change_log.change: Corrected the Ryu interpretation and distinguished the reviewed preprint from its linked journal publication.
change_log.reason: Optimized P-N effective ZT lies between constituent-leg values within the approximation; the additional hot-side wiring penalty specifically concerns single-leg devices.

change_log.change: Retained the reported SnSe numerical results and Lorenz-anomaly interpretation with explicit provenance and verification limits.
change_log.reason: The user requested preservation of useful quantitative detail and uncertainty. Missing retained artifacts prevent verification but do not justify treating earlier reports as false.

change_log.change: Removed the conclusion that the reported SnSe efficiency is well below half of Carnot.
change_log.reason: A temperature difference without absolute terminal temperatures cannot determine Carnot efficiency.

change_log.change: Preserved the withdrawn author attribution only as a limitation and supplied no replacement byline.
change_log.reason: Withdrawing an attribution does not verify the article's authorship.

change_log.change: Replaced the thermophotovoltaic numerical comparison and challenge ranking with an explicit scope limitation.
change_log.reason: Neither assertion has supporting evidence in the supplied artifacts.

change_log.change: Made durability uncertainty explicit and added temperature-span transport, power density, fabrication and replication requirements.
change_log.reason: These additions connect the proposed numerical milestones to reproducible module performance without presenting them as consensus standards.

change_log.change: Explained relationships to every other supplied roster entry while keeping each concept distinct.
change_log.reason: Related thermodynamic aims do not imply identical mechanisms or completion criteria.

unresolved_issues: The Science source needs retained text to verify the reported publication details, average ZT, conversion efficiency, device configuration, measurement boundary and absolute terminal temperatures.
The DOAJ-indexed article's authorship, publication details, Lorenz-number result, proposed scattering mechanism and artifact analysis remain unverified in the supplied review.

The review recommended removing the unverified experimental figures and interpretations. That recommendation was not adopted literally because the user requested preservation of useful research detail with explicit uncertainty; the claims are retained as earlier reports, not confirmed findings.
The supplied record does not establish whether the full THR-04 capability remains unrealized as of November 1, 2026.
The prevalence and operating regimes of known Wiedemann–Franz violations remain unestablished by the supplied evidence.
Application-specific minimum power density, fabrication yield, cost and broader lifetime requirements remain undefined.
The retained Ryu preprint supports the stated analytical conclusions, but the supplied review does not establish whether the journal version differs materially.
